narr: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of June 11th in an environment of strong afternoon heating as temperatures warmed into the low to mid 80s ahead of a backdoor cold front. CAPE values were in excess of 2,000 J/Kg and Precipitable Water values were observed to be in the 1.8 to 1.9 inch range. Weak atmospheric winds resulted in slow storm motion. The combination of deep instability and abundant moisture resulted in storms producing high rainfall rates of 2 to locally 5 inches per hour, with 1-hour rainfall totals exceeding 2.8 inches in the community of Stoneville. This rainfall is a 50-year event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates.
ev: Heavy rain, falling at rates of 2 to locally 5 inches per hour, caused the railroad underpass along Business Highway 220 to be flooded by several feet of standing water. The underpass was reopened after the water receded.
Runoff from heavy rain caused by a thunderstorm was observed flowing across Stone Mountain Road at M. P. Drive. No damage was reported and the road was reopened after the flood waters receded.

Runoff from heavy rain caused by a thunderstorm resulted in several inches of flowing water across S. Henry Street near the Adams Mart. No damage was reported and the road was passable after the flood waters receded.
